the use of PPCR is recommended for registration of contrast enhanced images when there is a large variation in enhancement intensity, particularly for breath-hold images, and that the use of direct fluid registration is recommended for registration when the contrast enhancement is small.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for breath-hold motion, PPCR is more successful than direct registration, but for breathing motion, PPCRs success is highly dependent on the level of contrast enhancement.
for breath-hold data with inconsistent depth, contrast-enhancement guided registration is more robust to the effects of organ motion.
the use of contrast-enhancement guided registration methods such as PPCR is recommended when the level of enhancement is high and the motion is not consistent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of image registration method depends on the type of organ motion and the level of contrast enhancement.
contrast enhancement and motion are interrelated, and must be considered together when designing registration algorithms.
motion and contrast-enhanced MRI are not independent, and that motion can affect registration results in a variety of ways.
